statements.subject: session
statements.description: Alice and Bob's media session has now begun, and they send media packets using the format to which they agreed in the exchange of SDP. (Labeled 'Media Session' in Figure 1.)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Alice confirms receipt of the BYE with a 200 (OK) response, which terminates the session and the BYE transaction.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Bob's SIP phone receives the INVITE and alerts Bob to the incoming call. Bob's SIP phone indicates this in a 180 (Ringing) response. When Alice's softphone receives the 180 (Ringing) response, it passes this information to Alice, perhaps using an audio ringback tone.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The transaction begins with Alice's softphone sending an INVITE request addressed to Bob's SIP URI. The proxy sends a 100 (Trying) response. Bob's SIP phone sends a 180 (Ringing) response routed back through the proxies.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When he picks up the handset, his SIP phone sends a 200 (OK) response to indicate that the call has been answered. Alice's softphone sends an acknowledgement message, ACK, to Bob's SIP phone to confirm the reception of the final response (200 (OK)). This completes the INVITE/200/ACK three-way handshake used to establish SIP sessions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If Bob did not wish to answer the call or was busy on another call, an error response would have been sent instead of the 200 (OK), which would have resulted in no media session being established.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Bob disconnects (hangs up) first and generates a BYE message. Alice confirms receipt of the BYE with a 200 (OK) response, which terminates the session and the BYE transaction.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: During the session, either Alice or Bob may decide to change the characteristics of the media session. This is accomplished by sending a re-INVITE containing a new media description. The other party sends a 200 (OK) to accept the change. The requestor responds to the 200 (OK) with an ACK.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the other party does not accept the change, he sends an error response such as 488 (Not Acceptable Here), which also receives an ACK. However, the failure of the re-INVITE does not cause the existing call to fail - the session continues using the previously negotiated characteristics.
actions: continue with previously negotiated session parameters

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The combination of the To tag, From tag, and Call-ID completely defines a peer-to-peer SIP relationship between Alice and Bob and is referred to as a dialog.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The combination of the To tag, From tag, and Call-ID completely defines a peer-to-peer SIP relationship between Alice and Bob and is referred to as a dialog.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The combination of the To tag, From tag, and Call-ID completely defines a peer-to-peer SIP relationship between Alice and Bob and is referred to as a dialog.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a TU wishes to send a request, it creates a client transaction instance and passes it the request along with the destination IP address, port, and transport to which to send the request.
actions: pass request with destination IP address, port, and transport

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a client cancels a transaction, it requests that the server stop further processing, revert to the state that existed before the transaction was initiated, and generate a specific error response to that transaction. This is done with a CANCEL request, which constitutes its own transaction, but references the transaction to be cancelled.
actions: revert to state that existed before transaction was initiated

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The INVITE method is the only way defined in this specification to establish a dialog. A dialog is a peer-to-peer SIP relationship between two user agents that persists for some time.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A dialog is a peer-to-peer SIP relationship between two UAs that persists for some time.
statements.invariant_cond: dialog.identified_by = call_id & dialog.local_tag != null & dialog.remote_tag != null

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A dialog is established by SIP messages, such as a 2xx response to an INVITE request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A SIP transaction occurs between a client and a server and comprises all messages from the first request sent from the client to the server up to a final (non-1xx) response sent from the server to the client.
statements.trigger: first request sent from client to server

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A final response terminates a SIP transaction, as opposed to a provisional response that does not. All 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx and 6xx responses are final.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A provisional response (1xx) does not terminate a SIP transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the request is INVITE and the final response is a non-2xx, the transaction also includes an ACK to the response.
statements.trigger: non-2xx final response to INVITE received
actions: send ACK to non-2xx final response

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The ACK for a 2xx response to an INVITE request is a separate transaction.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy is a logical entity that maintains the client and server transaction state machines defined by this specification during the processing of a request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless proxy is a logical entity that does not maintain the client or server transaction state machines defined in this specification when it processes requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A proxy is call stateful if it retains state for a dialog from the initiating INVITE to the terminating BYE request.
statements.invariant_cond: proxy.dialog_state_retained = true & dialog.initiated_by = INVITE & dialog.terminated_by_BYE = false

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A 2xx or 6xx class final response always terminates a sequential search.
statements.trigger: 2xx or 6xx final response received during sequential search

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client recurses on a 3xx response when it generates a new request to one or more of the URIs in the Contact header field in the response.
actions: generate new request to Contact URI(s) from 3xx response

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 1xx: Provisional -- request received, continuing to process the request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 2xx: Success -- the action was successfully received, understood, and accepted

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 3xx: Redirection -- further action needs to be taken in order to complete the request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 4xx: Client Error -- the request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled at this server

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 5xx: Server Error -- the server failed to fulfill an apparently valid request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: 6xx: Global Failure -- the request cannot be fulfilled at any server

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The initial Request-URI of the message SHOULD be set to the value of the URI in the To field.
statements.guard_semantics: initial request; method != REGISTER; no pre-existing route set

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a pre-existing route set is present, the procedures for populating the Request-URI and Route header field detailed in Section 12.2.1.1 MUST be followed (even though there is no dialog), using the desired Request-URI as the remote target URI.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A request outside of a dialog MUST NOT contain a To tag; the tag in the To field of a request identifies the peer of the dialog. Since no dialog is established, no tag is present.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The tag in the To field of a request identifies the peer of the dialog.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The From field MUST contain a new 'tag' parameter, chosen by the UAC.
statements.guard_semantics: Must be present and newly chosen by the UAC in every request

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UAC SHOULD use the display name 'Anonymous', along with a syntactically correct, but otherwise meaningless URI (like sip:thisis@anonymous.invalid), if the identity of the client is to remain hidden.
actions: set From URI to anonymous URI

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAC MUST insert a Max-Forwards header field into each request it originates with a value that SHOULD be 70.
statements.guard_semantics: must be present in every UAC-originated request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Max-Forwards value reaches 0 before the request reaches its destination, it will be rejected with a 483(Too Many Hops) error response.
actions: send 483 Too Many Hops error response

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The Via header field value MUST contain a branch parameter. This parameter is used to identify the transaction created by that request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A Via header field value is added only after the transport that will be used to reach the next hop has been selected.
actions: add Via header field value to request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When the UAC creates a request, it MUST insert a Via into that request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The branch parameter value MUST be unique across space and time for all requests sent by the UA. The exceptions to this rule are CANCEL and ACK for non-2xx responses.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A CANCEL request will have the same value of the branch parameter as the request it cancels.
actions: set CANCEL branch parameter equal to cancelled request branch parameter

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: An ACK for a non-2xx response will also have the same branch ID as the INVITE whose response it acknowledges.
actions: set ACK branch parameter equal to corresponding INVITE branch parameter

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The Contact header field MUST be present and contain exactly one SIP or SIPS URI in any request that can result in the establishment of a dialog. For the methods defined in this specification, that includes only the INVITE request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI or top Route header field value contains a SIPS URI, the Contact header field MUST contain a SIPS URI as well.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Each try constitutes a new transaction, and therefore each carries a different topmost Via header field value with a new branch parameter.
actions: set new branch parameter in topmost Via header field
set Via transport to transport determined for target server

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD follow the procedures defined in [4] for stateful elements, trying each address until a server is contacted. Each try constitutes a new transaction.
actions: select next ordered address from destination set
initiate new transaction to next address

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Each try constitutes a new transaction, and therefore each carries a different topmost Via header field value with a new branch parameter. Furthermore, the transport value in the Via header field is set to whatever transport was determined for the target server.
statements.guard_semantics: must be unique per transaction attempt; transport value must match transport determined for target server

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a timeout error is received from the transaction layer, it MUST be treated as if a 408 (Request Timeout) status code has been received.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a fatal transport error is reported by the transport layer (generally, due to fatal ICMP errors in UDP or connection failures in TCP), the condition MUST be treated as a 503 (Service Unavailable) status code.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAC MUST treat any final response it does not recognize as being equivalent to the x00 response code of that class, and MUST be able to process the x00 response code for all classes.
statements.pre_cond: response.code != null & response.code.recognized = false & response.class = final

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAC MUST treat any provisional response different than 100 that it does not recognize as 183 (Session Progress).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Upon receipt of a redirection response (for example, a 301 response status code), clients SHOULD use the URI(s) in the Contact header field to formulate one or more new requests based on the redirected request.
actions: place Contact URIs into target set
formulate new requests based on redirected request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client starts with an initial target set containing exactly one URI, the Request-URI of the original request.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As the target set grows, the client MAY generate new requests to the URIs in any order.
actions: generate new request to next URI in target set

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If contacting an address in the list results in a failure, the element moves to the next address in the list, until the list is exhausted.
actions: move to next address in target set

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the list is exhausted, then the request has failed.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the list is exhausted, then the request has failed.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Once the new request has been constructed, it is sent using a new client transaction, and therefore MUST have a new branch ID in the top Via field.
statements.guard_semantics: must be unique per new client transaction created on redirect

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client processing 3xx class responses MUST NOT add any given URI to the target set more than once.
statements.guard_semantics: each URI must appear at most once in the target set; prevents infinite redirection loops

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response is received, the UAC SHOULD follow the authorization procedures of Section 22.2 and Section 22.3 to retry the request with credentials.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 413 (Request Entity Too Large) response is received, the UAC SHOULD retry the request, either omitting the body or using one of a smaller length.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 415 (Unsupported Media Type) response is received, the UAC SHOULD retry sending the request, this time only using content with types listed in the Accept header field in the response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 416 (Unsupported URI Scheme) response is received, the client SHOULD retry the request, this time, using a SIP URI.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 420 (Bad Extension) response is received, the UAC SHOULD retry the request, this time omitting any extensions listed in the Unsupported header field in the response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: In all of the above cases, the request is retried by creating a new request with the appropriate modifications. This new request constitutes a new transaction and SHOULD have the same value of the Call-ID, To, and From of the previous request, but the CSeq should contain a new sequence number that is one higher than the previous.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a request is accepted, all state changes associated with it MUST be performed.
actions: perform all state changes associated with the request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a request is rejected, all state changes MUST NOT be performed.
actions: revert all state changes associated with the request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Request processing is atomic. If a request is accepted, all state changes associated with it MUST be performed. If it is rejected, all state changes MUST NOT be performed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Once a request is authenticated (or authentication is skipped), the UAS MUST inspect the method of the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the UAS recognizes but does not support the method of a request, it MUST generate a 405 (Method Not Allowed) response. The UAS MUST also add an Allow header field to the 405 response.
actions: add Allow header field to 405 response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the method is one supported by the server, processing continues.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The UAS MUST also add an Allow header field to the 405 (Method Not Allowed) response. The Allow header field MUST list the set of methods supported by the UAS generating the message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the UAS decides to reject the request (based on To header field policy), it SHOULD generate a response with a 403 (Forbidden) status code and pass it to the server transaction for transmission.
actions: pass response to server transaction for transmission

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI uses a scheme not supported by the UAS, it SHOULD reject the request with a 416 (Unsupported URI Scheme) response.
actions: reject request with 416 Unsupported URI Scheme response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI does not identify an address that the UAS is willing to accept requests for, it SHOULD reject the request with a 404 (Not Found) response.
actions: reject request with 404 Not Found response

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the request has no tag in the To header field, the UAS core MUST check the request against ongoing transactions. If the From tag, Call-ID, and CSeq exactly match those associated with an ongoing transaction, but the request does not match that transaction (based on the matching rules in Section 17.2.3), the UAS core SHOULD generate a 482 (Loop Detected) response and pass it to the server transaction.
statements.pre_cond: request.To.tag = null & request.From_tag = ongoing_transaction.From_tag & request.Call_ID = ongoing_transaction.Call_ID & request.CSeq = ongoing_transaction.CSeq & request.match_section_17_2_3 = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a UAS does not understand an option-tag listed in a Require header field, it MUST respond by generating a response with status code 420 (Bad Extension). The UAS MUST add an Unsupported header field, and list in it those options it does not understand amongst those in the Require header field of the request.
statements.trigger: unrecognized option-tag in Require header field
actions: add Unsupported header field listing unrecognized option-tags

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Require and Proxy-Require MUST NOT be used in a SIP CANCEL request, or in an ACK request sent for a non-2xx response. These header fields MUST be ignored if they are present in these requests.
statements.trigger: CANCEL or non-2xx ACK received with Require or Proxy-Require header
statements.pre_cond: (message.method = CANCEL | (message.method = ACK & response.status_code != 2xx)) & (message.Require != null | message.Proxy-Require != null)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An ACK request for a 2xx response MUST contain only those Require and Proxy-Require values that were present in the initial request.
statements.allowed_values: values present in the initial INVITE request only

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An ACK request for a 2xx response MUST contain only those Require and Proxy-Require values that were present in the initial request.
statements.allowed_values: values present in the initial INVITE request only

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there are any bodies whose type, language, or encoding are not understood, and that body part is not optional, the UAS MUST reject the request with a 415 (Unsupported Media Type) response.
statements.pre_cond: body.content_type.understood = false | body.content_language.understood = false | body.content_encoding.understood = false & body.content_disposition.optional = false
actions: include Accept header listing understood body types if request contained unsupported content types
include Accept-Encoding header listing understood encodings if request contained unsupported content encodings
include Accept-Language header listing understood languages if request contained unsupported content languages

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Once all procedures associated with the creation of a response have been completed, the UAS hands the response back to the server transaction from which it received the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: UASs SHOULD NOT issue a provisional response for a non-INVITE request. Rather, UASs SHOULD generate a final response to a non-INVITE request as soon as possible.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a 100 (Trying) response is generated, any Timestamp header field present in the request MUST be copied into this 100 (Trying) response.
actions: copy Timestamp header from request to 100 Trying response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is a delay in generating the response, the UAS SHOULD add a delay value into the Timestamp value in the response. This value MUST contain the difference between the time of sending of the response and receipt of the request, measured in seconds.
actions: add delay value to Timestamp in 100 Trying response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the To header field in the request did not contain a tag, the UAS MUST add a tag to the To header field in the response (with the exception of the 100 (Trying) response, in which a tag MAY be present).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The same tag MUST be used for all responses to that request, both final and provisional (again excepting the 100 (Trying)).
statements.guard_semantics: response.To-tag = initial_response.To-tag for all responses where response.status != 100

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the To header field in the request did not contain a tag, the UAS MUST add a tag to the To header field in the response (with the exception of the 100 (Trying) response, in which a tag MAY be present). This serves to identify the UAS that is responding, possibly resulting in a component of a dialog ID.
statements.trigger: send non-100 response when request.To-tag absent
actions: add To-tag to response To header field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a request contained a To tag in the request, the To header field in the response MUST equal that of the request.
actions: copy To header field from request to response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS is a UAS that does not maintain transaction state. It replies to requests normally, but discards any state that would ordinarily be retained by a UAS after a response has been sent.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A UAS can operate in either a stateful or stateless mode for each new request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Stateless UASs do not use a transaction layer; they receive requests directly from the transport layer and send responses directly to the transport layer.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a stateless UAS receives a retransmission of a request, it regenerates the response and resends it, just as if it were replying to the first instance of the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST NOT send provisional (1xx) responses.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST NOT retransmit responses.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST ignore ACK requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST ignore CANCEL requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To header tags MUST be generated for responses in a stateless manner - in a manner that will generate the same tag for the same request consistently.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The redirect server maintains transaction state for an entire SIP transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This response ends the SIP transaction.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After receiving a request other than CANCEL, the server either refuses the request or gathers the list of alternative locations from the location service and returns a final response of class 3xx.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For well-formed CANCEL requests, it SHOULD return a 2xx response. This response ends the SIP transaction.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Redirect servers MUST NOT redirect a request to a URI equal to the one in the Request-URI; instead, provided that the URI does not point to itself, the server MAY proxy the request to the destination URI, or MAY reject it with a 404.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a redirect server returns a 3xx response to a request, it populates the list of (one or more) alternative locations into the Contact header field.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAS that receives a CANCEL request for an INVITE, but has not yet sent a final response, would 'stop ringing', and then respond to the INVITE with a specific error response (a 487).

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: CANCEL has no effect on a request to which a UAS has already given a final response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: CANCEL asks the UAS to cease processing the request and to generate an error response to that request.
statements.guard_semantics: Determines whether CANCEL has any effect on the target transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy responds to a CANCEL, rather than simply forwarding a response it would receive from a downstream element. CANCEL is referred to as a 'hop-by-hop' request, since it is responded to at each stateful proxy hop.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: the client SHOULD then consider the original transaction cancelled

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: the client MUST wait for the arrival of a provisional response before sending the CANCEL request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If no provisional response has been received, the CANCEL request MUST NOT be sent; rather, the client MUST wait for the arrival of a provisional response before sending the request.
actions: defer CANCEL transmission until provisional response received

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the client decides to send the CANCEL, it creates a client transaction for the CANCEL and passes it the CANCEL request along with the destination address, port, and transport.
actions: pass CANCEL request with destination address, port, and transport

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the original request has generated a final response, the CANCEL SHOULD NOT be sent, as it is an effective no-op, since CANCEL has no effect on requests that have already generated a final response.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If there is no final response for the original request in 64*T1 seconds, the client SHOULD then consider the original transaction cancelled and SHOULD destroy the client transaction handling the original request.
actions: destroy client transaction handling original request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the UAS did not find a matching transaction for the CANCEL according to the procedure above, it SHOULD respond to the CANCEL with a 481 (Call Leg/Transaction Does Not Exist).
statements.trigger: CANCEL received, no matching transaction found

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the transaction for the original request still exists and the UAS has already sent a final response for the original request, the CANCEL request has no effect on the processing of the original request, no effect on any session state, and no effect on the responses generated for the original request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the UAS has not issued a final response for the original request and the original request was an INVITE, the UAS SHOULD immediately respond to the INVITE with a 487 (Request Terminated).
statements.pre_cond: transaction.matching = true & transaction.final_response_sent = false & transaction.method = INVITE

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Regardless of the method of the original request, as long as the CANCEL matched an existing transaction, the UAS answers the CANCEL request itself with a 200 (OK) response. The response to CANCEL is passed to the server transaction for transmission.
actions: pass 200 OK to server transaction for transmission

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The To tag of the response to the CANCEL and the To tag in the response to the original request SHOULD be the same.
statements.guard_semantics: must equal To tag of original request response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A REGISTER request does not establish a dialog.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: UAs MUST NOT send a new registration (that is, containing new Contact header field values, as opposed to a retransmission) until they have received a final response from the registrar for the previous one or the previous REGISTER request has timed out.
statements.trigger: new REGISTER with new Contact values

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: UAs MUST NOT send a new registration until they have received a final response from the registrar for the previous one.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: UAs MUST NOT send a new registration until the previous REGISTER request has timed out.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The CSeq value guarantees proper ordering of REGISTER requests. A UA MUST increment the CSeq value by one for each REGISTER request with the same Call-ID.
statements.guard_semantics: incremented by 1 per REGISTER with same Call-ID; enables registrar to detect out-of-order delivery

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The REGISTER request sent to a registrar includes the contact address(es) to which SIP requests for the address-of-record should be forwarded. The address-of-record is included in the To header field of the REGISTER request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The 2xx response to the REGISTER request will contain, in a Contact header field, a complete list of bindings that have been registered for this address-of-record at this registrar.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a client has established bindings at a registrar, it MAY send subsequent registrations containing new bindings or modifications to existing bindings as necessary.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the address-of-record in the To header field of a REGISTER request is a SIPS URI, then any Contact header field values in the request SHOULD also be SIPS URIs.
statements.guard_semantics: message.To = SIPS_URI => message.Contact SHOULD be SIPS_URI

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UA requests the immediate removal of a binding by specifying an expiration interval of '0' for that contact address in a REGISTER request.
statements.trigger: REGISTER request with expiration interval 0 for contact address
actions: remove binding for specified contact address

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The REGISTER-specific Contact header field value of '*' MUST NOT be used unless the Expires header field is present with a value of '0'.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Use of the '*' Contact header field value allows a registering UA to remove all bindings associated with an address-of-record without knowing their precise values.
statements.trigger: REGISTER request with Contact=* and Expires=0
actions: remove all bindings associated with address-of-record

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The 200 (OK) response from the registrar contains a list of Contact fields enumerating all current bindings. The UA compares each contact address to see if it created the contact address. If so, it updates the expiration time interval according to the expires parameter or, if absent, the Expires field value.
actions: compare each contact address against created contact addresses
update expiration time interval per expires parameter or Expires field value

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The UA then issues a REGISTER request for each of its bindings before the expiration interval has elapsed. It MAY combine several updates into one REGISTER request.
actions: send REGISTER request for binding before expiration interval elapses

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Registration refreshes SHOULD be sent to the same network address as the original registration, unless redirected.
actions: send REGISTER refresh to same network address as original registration

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UA SHOULD use the same Call-ID for all registrations during a single boot cycle.
allowed_values: same value as original registration Call-ID within boot cycle

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the transaction layer returns a timeout error because the REGISTER yielded no response, the UAC SHOULD NOT immediately re-attempt a registration to the same registrar.
statements.trigger: transaction layer timeout error (no response to REGISTER)
actions: suppress immediate re-registration attempt to same registrar

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a UA receives a 423 (Interval Too Brief) response, it MAY retry the registration after making the expiration interval of all contact addresses in the REGISTER request equal to or greater than the expiration interval within the Min-Expires header field of the 423 (Interval Too Brief) response.
actions: set all contact address expiration intervals to >= Min-Expires value

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the registrar does not have access to bindings for the domain identified in the Request-URI, and if the server also acts as a proxy server, the server SHOULD forward the request to the addressed domain.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the authenticated user is not authorized to modify bindings, the registrar MUST return a 403 (Forbidden) and skip the remaining steps.

If the session description has changed, the UAS MUST adjust the session parameters accordingly.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the new session description is not acceptable, the UAS can reject it by returning a 488 (Not Acceptable Here) response for the re-INVITE. This response SHOULD include a Warning header field.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a UAS generates a 2xx response and never receives an ACK, it SHOULD generate a BYE to terminate the dialog.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If, however, it is unacceptable to the UAC, the UAC SHOULD generate an answer with a valid session description, and then send a BYE to terminate the session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The caller's UA MAY send a BYE for either confirmed or early dialogs, and the callee's UA MAY send a BYE on confirmed dialogs, but MUST NOT send a BYE on early dialogs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The caller's UA MAY send a BYE for either confirmed or early dialogs, and the callee's UA MAY send a BYE on confirmed dialogs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If an initial INVITE generates a non-2xx final response, that terminates all sessions (if any) and all dialogs (if any) that were created through responses to the request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If an initial INVITE generates a non-2xx final response, that terminates all sessions (if any) and all dialogs (if any) that were created through responses to the request.
statements.trigger: non-2xx final response to INVITE received
actions: terminate all sessions created by INVITE
terminate all dialogs created by INVITE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a BYE is received on a dialog, any session associated with that dialog SHOULD terminate.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If no SIP extensions have defined other application layer states associated with the dialog, the BYE also terminates the dialog.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The caller's UA MAY send a BYE for either confirmed or early dialogs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: the callee's UA MAY send a BYE on confirmed dialogs, but MUST NOT send a BYE on early dialogs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: the callee's UA MUST NOT send a BYE on a confirmed dialog until it has received an ACK for its 2xx response or until the server transaction times out.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The CANCEL attempts to force a non-2xx response to the INVITE (in particular, a 487). Therefore, if a UAC wishes to give up on its call attempt entirely, it can send a CANCEL.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the INVITE results in 2xx final response(s) to the INVITE, this means that a UAS accepted the invitation while the CANCEL was in progress. The UAC MAY continue with the sessions established by any 2xx responses, or MAY terminate them with BYE.
statements.trigger: 2xx response received while CANCEL in progress

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UA MUST NOT send a BYE outside of a dialog.
statements.guard_semantics: BYE may only be sent when an established dialog exists

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The UAC MUST consider the session terminated (and therefore stop sending or listening for media) as soon as the BYE request is passed to the client transaction.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The UAC MUST consider the session terminated (and therefore stop sending or listening for media) as soon as the BYE request is passed to the client transaction.
statements.trigger: BYE request passed to client transaction

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the response for the BYE is a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) or a 408 (Request Timeout) or no response at all is received for the BYE (that is, a timeout is returned by the client transaction), the UAC MUST consider the session and the dialog terminated.
statements.trigger: 481 response | 408 response | transaction timeout received for BYE

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Once the BYE is constructed, the UAC core creates a new non-INVITE client transaction, and passes it the BYE request.
actions: pass BYE request to client transaction

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A UAS core receiving a BYE request checks if it matches an existing dialog. If the BYE does not match an existing dialog, the UAS core SHOULD generate a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) response and pass that to the server transaction.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UAS core receiving a BYE request for an existing dialog MUST follow the procedures of Section 12.2.2 to process the request. Once done, the UAS SHOULD terminate the session (and therefore stop sending and listening for media). The UAS core MUST generate a 2xx response to the BYE, and MUST pass that to the server transaction for transmission.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The UAS MUST still respond to any pending requests received for that dialog. It is RECOMMENDED that a 487 (Request Terminated) response be generated to those pending requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When stateless, a proxy acts as a simple forwarding element. It forwards each request downstream to a single element determined by making a targeting and routing decision based on the request. A stateless proxy discards information about a message once the message has been forwarded.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy remembers information (specifically, transaction state) about each incoming request and any requests it sends as a result of processing the incoming request. It uses this information to affect the processing of future messages associated with that request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy MAY transition to stateless operation at any time during the processing of a request, so long as it did not do anything that would otherwise prevent it from being stateless initially (forking, for example, or generation of a 100 response). When performing such a transition, all state is simply discarded. The proxy SHOULD NOT initiate a CANCEL request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy MAY choose to 'fork' a request, routing it to multiple destinations. Any request that is forwarded to more than one location MUST be handled statefully.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a request arrives, an element that can play the role of a proxy first decides if it needs to respond to the request on its own. The element MAY respond with any appropriate error code. When responding directly to a request, the element is playing the role of a UAS and MUST behave as described in Section 8.2.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy creates a new server transaction for each new request received. Any retransmissions of the request will then be handled by that server transaction per Section 17.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: An incoming request is processed by a server transaction. Requests from the server transaction are passed to a proxy core.
statements.trigger: incoming request arrives at server transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The proxy core determines where to route the request, choosing one or more next-hop locations. An outgoing request for each next-hop location is processed by its own associated client transaction.
statements.trigger: proxy core receives request from server transaction
actions: forward outgoing request via client transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The proxy core collects the responses from the client transactions and uses them to send responses to the server transaction.
actions: proxy core collects response from client transaction

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy core MUST behave as a UAS with respect to sending an immediate provisional on that server transaction (such as 100 Trying) as described in Section 8.2.6.
statements.trigger: new INVITE request received by server transaction

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy SHOULD NOT generate 100 (Trying) responses to non-INVITE requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For all new requests, including any with unknown methods, an element intending to proxy the request MUST: 1. Validate the request, 2. Preprocess routing information, 3. Determine target(s), 4. Forward the request to each target, 5. Process all responses.
actions: forward the request to each target (Section 16.6)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If any of these checks fail, the element MUST behave as a user agent server (see Section 8.2) and respond with an error code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI has a URI whose scheme is not understood by the proxy, the proxy SHOULD reject the request with a 416 (Unsupported URI Scheme) response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request contains a Max-Forwards header field with a field value of zero (0), the element MUST NOT forward the request. If the request was for OPTIONS, the element MAY act as the final recipient and respond per Section 11.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request contains a Max-Forwards header field with a field value of zero (0), the element MUST NOT forward the request. Otherwise, the element MUST return a 483 (Too many hops) response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a loop is detected, the element MAY return a 482 (Loop Detected) response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request contains a Proxy-Require header field with one or more option-tags this element does not understand, the element MUST return a 420 (Bad Extension) response. The response MUST include an Unsupported header field listing those option-tags the element did not understand.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A valid message must pass the following checks: 1. Reasonable Syntax, 2. URI scheme, 3. Max-Forwards, 4. (Optional) Loop Detection, 5. Proxy-Require, 6. Proxy-Authorization

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI of the request contains a value this proxy previously placed into a Record-Route header field, the proxy MUST replace the Request-URI in the request with the last value from the Route header field, and remove that value from the Route header field. The proxy MUST then proceed as if it received this modified request.
statements.trigger: Request-URI matches previously placed Record-Route value
actions: replace Request-URI with last Route header field value
remove that value from Route header field
proceed as if modified request was received

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI has a maddr parameter with a value the proxy is responsible for, and the request was received using the port and transport indicated in the Request-URI, the proxy MUST strip the maddr and any non-default port or transport parameter and continue processing as if those values had not been present in the request.
statements.trigger: Request-URI maddr matches proxy-responsible address and port/transport match
statements.pre_cond: request.request_uri.maddr = proxy.responsible_address & request.received_port = request.request_uri.port & request.received_transport = request.request_uri.transport
statements.post_cond: request.request_uri.maddr = null & request.request_uri.non_default_port = null & request.request_uri.non_default_transport = null
actions: strip any non-default port parameter from Request-URI
strip any non-default transport parameter from Request-URI

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the first value in the Route header field indicates this proxy, the proxy MUST remove that value from the request.
statements.trigger: first Route header value identifies this proxy
actions: remove first Route header field value from request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Next, the proxy calculates the target(s) of the request. The set of targets will either be predetermined by the contents of the request or will be obtained from an abstract location service.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI of the request contains an maddr parameter, the Request-URI MUST be placed into the target set as the only target URI, and the proxy MUST proceed to Section 16.6.
actions: place Request-URI into target set as only target URI

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the domain of the Request-URI indicates a domain this element is not responsible for, the Request-URI MUST be placed into the target set as the only target, and the element MUST proceed to the task of Request Forwarding (Section 16.6).
actions: place Request-URI into target set as only target

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI does not provide sufficient information for the proxy to determine the target set, it SHOULD return a 485 (Ambiguous) response.
statements.trigger: Request-URI insufficient to determine target set

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the Request-URI indicates a resource at this proxy that does not exist, the proxy MUST return a 404 (Not Found) response.
statements.trigger: Request-URI resource does not exist at proxy

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the target set remains empty after applying all of the above, the proxy MUST return an error response, which SHOULD be the 480 (Temporarily Unavailable) response.
statements.trigger: target set empty after all determination steps

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Targets can only be placed in the target set once. If a target URI is already present in the set (based on the definition of equality for the URI type), it MUST NOT be added again.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A proxy MUST NOT add additional targets to the target set if the Request-URI of the original request does not indicate a resource this proxy is responsible for.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy must have a mechanism to maintain the target set as responses are received and associate the responses to each forwarded request with the original request. For the purposes of this model, this mechanism is a 'response context' created by the proxy layer before forwarding the first request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: As soon as the target set is non-empty, a proxy MAY begin forwarding the request. A stateful proxy MUST create a new client transaction for this request and instructs the transaction to send the request using the address, port and transport determined in step 7.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the client transaction reports failure to send the request or a timeout from its state machine, the proxy continues to the next address in that ordered set.
actions: continue to next address in ordered set
create new client transaction for next tuple

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the ordered set is exhausted, the request cannot be forwarded to this element in the target set. The proxy does not need to place anything in the response context, but otherwise acts as if this element of the target set returned a 408 (Request Timeout) final response.
actions: treat target element as returning 408 Request Timeout final response

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Timer C MUST be set for each client transaction when an INVITE request is proxied. The timer MUST be larger than 3 minutes.
actions: set timer C with value greater than 3 minutes

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Section 16.7 bullet 2 discusses how this timer is updated with provisional responses, and Section 16.8 discusses processing when it fires.
actions: process timer C expiry per Section 16.8

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Since each attempt uses a new client transaction, it represents a new branch. Thus, the branch parameter provided with the Via header field inserted in step 8 MUST be different for each attempt.
actions: insert Via with unique branch parameter

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A pending client transaction is one that has received a provisional response, but no final response (it is in the proceeding state) and has not had an associated CANCEL generated for it.
statements.invariant_cond: transaction.provisional_received = true & transaction.final_received = false & transaction.cancel_generated = false

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a response is received by an element, it first tries to locate a client transaction matching the response. If none is found, the element MUST process the response (even if it is an informational response) as a stateless proxy.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a match is found, the response is handed to the client transaction.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For an INVITE transaction, if the response is a provisional response with status codes 101 to 199 inclusive, the proxy MUST reset timer C for that client transaction. The timer MAY be reset to a different value, but this value MUST be greater than 3 minutes.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If no Via header field values remain in the response, the response was meant for this element and MUST NOT be forwarded. The UAC processing rules described in Section 8.1.3 are followed instead.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a 6xx response is received, it is not immediately forwarded, but the stateful proxy SHOULD cancel all client pending transactions as described in Section 10, and it MUST NOT create any new branches in this context.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy MUST send a final response to a response context's server transaction if no final responses have been immediately forwarded by the above rules and all client transactions in this response context have been terminated.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If there are no final responses in the context, the proxy MUST send a 408 (Request Timeout) response to the server transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the forwarded response was a final response, the proxy MUST generate a CANCEL request for all pending client transactions associated with this response context. A proxy SHOULD also generate a CANCEL request for all pending client transactions associated with this response context when it receives a 6xx response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A pending client transaction is one that has received a provisional response, but no final response (it is in the proceeding state) and has not had an associated CANCEL generated for it.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The proxy MUST maintain the response context until all of its associated transactions have been terminated, even after forwarding a final response.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If timer C should fire, the proxy MUST either reset the timer with any value it chooses, or terminate the client transaction.
actions: reset Timer C with chosen value

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If timer C should fire and the client transaction has received a provisional response, the proxy MUST generate a CANCEL request matching that transaction.
statements.post_cond: CANCEL request generated matching client transaction
actions: generate CANCEL request matching client transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If timer C should fire and the client transaction has not received a provisional response, the proxy MUST behave as if the transaction received a 408 (Request Timeout) response.
actions: treat transaction as if 408 Request Timeout response received

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the transport layer notifies a proxy of an error when it tries to forward a request, the proxy MUST behave as if the forwarded request received a 503 (Service Unavailable) response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the proxy is notified of an error when forwarding a response, it drops the response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The proxy SHOULD NOT cancel any outstanding client transactions associated with this response context due to this notification.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A proxy MUST cancel any pending client transactions associated with a response context when it receives a matching CANCEL request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a matching response context is found, the element MUST immediately return a 200 (OK) response to the CANCEL request. Furthermore, the element MUST generate CANCEL requests for all pending client transactions in the context.
actions: generate CANCEL for all pending client transactions in response context

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a response context is not found, the element does not have any knowledge of the request to apply the CANCEL to. It MUST statelessly forward the CANCEL request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy MAY generate CANCEL requests for pending INVITE client transactions based on the period specified in the INVITE's Expires header field elapsing.
statements.pre_cond: transaction.state = pending & transaction.method = INVITE & provisional_response_received = true
actions: generate CANCEL for pending INVITE client transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateful proxy MAY generate a CANCEL to any other request it has generated at any time (subject to receiving a provisional response to that request).
actions: generate CANCEL request for pending client transaction

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A stateless proxy does not have any notion of a transaction, or of the response context used to describe stateful proxy behavior.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When handling a request statelessly, an element MUST NOT generate its own 100 (Trying) or any other provisional response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless proxy MUST validate a request as described in Section 16.3 and MUST follow the request processing steps described in Sections 16.4 through 16.5; the request is sent directly to the transport layer instead of through a client transaction.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless proxy MUST choose one and only one target from the target set. This choice MUST only rely on fields in the message and time-invariant properties of the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a response arrives at a stateless proxy, the proxy MUST inspect the sent-by value in the first (topmost) Via header field value. If that address matches the proxy, the proxy MUST remove that header field value from the response and forward the result to the location indicated in the next Via header field value.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the address does not match the proxy, the message MUST be silently discarded.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Stateless proxies MUST NOT perform special processing for CANCEL requests. They are processed by the above rules as any other requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI indicates a resource owned by this proxy, the proxy will replace it with the results of running a location service. Otherwise, the proxy will not change the Request-URI.
actions: replace Request-URI with location service result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the URI in the topmost Route header field value indicates this proxy, the proxy removes it from the Route header field (this route node has been reached).
actions: remove topmost Route header field value

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy will forward the request to the resource indicated by the URI in the topmost Route header field value or in the Request-URI if no Route header field is present.
actions: determine address/port/transport from topmost Route URI or Request-URI

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The callee at u2.domain.com gets this and responds with a 200 OK. The callee at u2 also sets its dialog state's remote target URI to sip:caller@u1.example.com and its route set to (<sip:p2.domain.com;lr>,<sip:p1.example.com;lr>).
actions: set dialog.remote_target_uri from Contact header of received INVITE
set dialog.route_set from Record-Route headers of received INVITE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The callee at u2 sets its dialog state's remote target URI to sip:caller@u1.example.com and its route set to (<sip:p2.domain.com;lr>,<sip:p1.example.com;lr>).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The callee at u2 sets its dialog state's route set to (<sip:p2.domain.com;lr>,<sip:p1.example.com;lr>).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The 200 OK is forwarded by P2 to P1 to U1 as normal. Now, U1 sets its dialog state's remote target URI to sip:callee@u2.domain.com and its route set to (<sip:p1.example.com;lr>,<sip:p2.domain.com;lr>).
actions: set dialog.remote_target_uri from Contact header of received 200 OK
set dialog.route_set from Record-Route headers of received 200 OK

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Since all the route set elements contain the lr parameter, U1 constructs the following BYE request with Request-URI = dialog.remote_target_uri and Route set from dialog.route_set.
actions: set BYE Route header from dialog.route_set
resolve topmost Route entry via DNS to determine next hop

statements.subject: server
statements.description: P1 notices that it is not responsible for the resource indicated in the Request-URI so it doesn't change it. It does see that it is the first value in the Route header field, so it removes that value, and forwards the request to P2.
statements.trigger: receive BYE with self as topmost Route value
actions: remove self from topmost Route header field value
forward request to next Route entry

statements.subject: server
statements.description: P2 also notices it is not responsible for the resource indicated by the Request-URI, so it doesn't change it. It does see itself in the first Route header field value, so it removes it and forwards to u2.domain.com based on a DNS lookup against the Request-URI.
statements.trigger: receive BYE with self as topmost Route value
actions: remove self from topmost Route header field value
forward request to destination resolved from Request-URI

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: P4 notices that it is the element in the first Route header field value so it removes it. It then prepares to send the request based on the now first Route header field value, but notices this URI does not contain the lr parameter, so before sending, it reformats the request placing the original Request-URI at the end of the Route list and putting the strict-router address in the Request-URI.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: P3 is a strict router, so it forwards the following to P2: it places the first Route header value into the Request-URI and appends the old Request-URI to the end of the Route list.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: P2 sees the request-URI is a value it placed into a Record-Route header field, so before further processing, it rewrites the request restoring the original Request-URI and removes its own value from the Route list.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: P1 notices itself in the topmost Route header field value, so it removes it. Since P1 is not responsible for u1.example.com and there is no Route header field, P1 will forward the request to u1.example.com based on the Request-URI.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: In the case of a transaction where the request was an INVITE (known as an INVITE transaction), the transaction also includes the ACK only if the final response was not a 2xx response. If the response was a 2xx, the ACK is not considered part of the transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The client transaction is responsible for receiving responses and delivering them to the TU, filtering out any response retransmissions or disallowed responses (such as a response to ACK).

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: In the case of an INVITE request, the client transaction is responsible for generating the ACK request for any final response excepting a 2xx response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The server transaction filters any request retransmissions from the network. In the case of an INVITE transaction, it absorbs the ACK request for any final response excepting a 2xx response.
actions: absorb ACK when transaction.method = INVITE & final_response.code != 2xx

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Retransmissions of the 2xx response are handled by the UA core, not the transaction layer. Similarly, generation of the ACK for the 2xx is handled by the UA core.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: One handles client transactions for INVITE requests. This type of machine is referred to as an INVITE client transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Another type handles client transactions for all requests except INVITE and ACK. This is referred to as a non-INVITE client transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: There are two types of client transaction state machines, depending on the method of the request passed by the TU: INVITE client transaction and non-INVITE client transaction. There is no client transaction for ACK.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When the TU wishes to initiate a new transaction, it creates a client transaction and passes it the SIP request to send and an IP address, port, and transport to which to send it. The client transaction begins execution of its state machine.
actions: pass SIP request to client transaction
provide IP address, port, and transport

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Valid responses are passed up to the TU from the client transaction.
actions: pass valid response up to TU

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the TU wishes to send an ACK, it passes one directly to the transport layer for transmission. There is no client transaction for ACK.
actions: pass ACK directly to transport layer

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: After receiving a 1xx response, any retransmissions cease altogether, and the client waits for further responses.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: For each final response that is received at the client transaction, the client transaction sends an ACK, the purpose of which is to quench retransmissions of the response.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For unreliable transports (such as UDP), the client transaction retransmits requests at an interval that starts at T1 seconds and doubles after every retransmission. T1 is an estimate of the round-trip time (RTT), and it defaults to 500 ms.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The request is not retransmitted over reliable transports.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: For unreliable transports, that response is retransmitted periodically, and for reliable transports, it is sent once.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The initial state, 'calling', MUST be entered when the TU initiates a new client transaction with an INVITE request.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the client transaction receives a provisional response while in the 'Calling' state, it transitions to the 'Proceeding' state. In the 'Proceeding' state, the client transaction SHOULD NOT retransmit the request any longer.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Reception of a response with status code from 300-699 MUST cause the client transaction to transition to 'Completed'.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The client transaction MUST be destroyed the instant it enters the 'Terminated' state.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The initial state, 'calling', MUST be entered when the TU initiates a new client transaction with an INVITE request. The client transaction MUST pass the request to the transport layer for transmission. If unreliable transport, start Timer A with T1; for any transport, start Timer B with 64*T1.
actions: start Timer A with T1 (unreliable transport only)

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When timer A fires, the client transaction MUST retransmit the request by passing it to the transport layer, and MUST reset the timer with a value of 2*T1. Retransmission intervals MUST double after each transmission.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the client transaction is still in the 'Calling' state when timer B fires, the client transaction SHOULD inform the TU that a timeout has occurred. The client transaction MUST NOT generate an ACK.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Transport Error while in Calling state causes transition to Terminated; inform TU. (From Figure 5: right-side arrow from Calling labeled 'Timer B fires or Transport Err. / inform TU'.)

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the client transaction receives a provisional response while in the 'Calling' state, it transitions to the 'Proceeding' state. The provisional response MUST be passed to the TU.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When in the 'Calling' state, reception of a response with status code from 300-699 MUST cause the client transaction to transition to 'Completed'. The client transaction MUST pass the received response up to the TU, and MUST generate an ACK request and pass it to the transport layer. Timer D SHOULD be started.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When in the 'Calling' state, reception of a 2xx response MUST cause the client transaction to enter the 'Terminated' state, and the response MUST be passed up to the TU.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Any further provisional responses MUST be passed up to the TU while in the 'Proceeding' state.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When in the 'Proceeding' state, reception of a response with status code from 300-699 MUST cause the client transaction to transition to 'Completed'. The client transaction MUST pass the received response up to the TU, and MUST generate an ACK request and pass it to the transport layer. Timer D SHOULD be started.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When in the 'Proceeding' state, reception of a 2xx response MUST cause the client transaction to enter the 'Terminated' state, and the response MUST be passed up to the TU.

statements.subject: transaction

statements.description: In SIP, a UAS uses the 401 (Unauthorized) response to challenge the identity of a UAC.

statements.description: registrars and redirect servers MAY make use of 401 (Unauthorized) responses for authentication, but proxies MUST NOT, and instead MAY use the 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response.

statements.description: Servers MUST NOT attempt to challenge an ACK.

statements.subject: transaction

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no credentials (in the Proxy-Authorization header field) are provided in the request, the proxy can challenge the originator to provide credentials by rejecting the request with a 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) status code.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: All 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) responses MUST be forwarded upstream toward the UAC following the procedures for any other response.

statements.description: When the originating UAC receives the 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) it SHOULD, if it is able, re-originate the request with the proper credentials.

statements.description: If no credentials for a realm can be located, UACs MAY attempt to retry the request with a username of 'anonymous' and no password (a password of '').

aggregate all Proxy-Authenticate values into single response
send single aggregated response to UAC

actions: include Authorization value per WWW-Authenticate challenge
include Proxy-Authorization value per Proxy-Authenticate challenge

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD also cache the credentials used in the re-originated request.

statements.subject: user
statements.description: If a UA receives an S/MIME body that has been encrypted with a public key unknown to the recipient, it MUST reject the request with a 493 (Undecipherable) response.

statements.subject: user

actions: include certificate in 493 response body with smime-type=certs-only

statements.subject: user

statements.description: If there is a discrepancy [between offered and stored certificate], the UA MUST notify its user of a change of the certificate and acquire the user's permission before continuing to process the signaling.

actions: notify user that remote device does not support S/MIME

statements.description: If a user agent sends an S/MIME body in a request, but receives a response that contains a MIME body that is not secured, the UAC SHOULD notify its user that the session could not be secured.
actions: notify user that session could not be secured

statements.subject: user

actions: notify user of certificate change indicating potential security breach

statements.subject: user
statements.description: State in which a UA has received a certificate requiring user decision before processing can continue — triggered by unverifiable or mismatched certificates.

statements.description: The registrar SHOULD offer a certificate to the UA; when it receives the TLS Certificate message, the UA SHOULD verify the certificate and inspect the site identified by the certificate.

statements.description: If the certificate is invalid, revoked, or if it does not identify the appropriate party, the UA MUST NOT send the REGISTER message and otherwise proceed with the registration.

statements.description: The UA then creates a REGISTER request that SHOULD be addressed to a Request-URI corresponding to the site certificate received from the registrar. When the UA sends the REGISTER request over the existing TLS connection...

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The registrar SHOULD challenge the request with a 401 (Proxy Authentication Required) response. When the UAC receives the challenge, it SHOULD either prompt the user for credentials or take an appropriate credential from a keyring.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Once the Digest credentials have been inserted into an appropriate Proxy-Authorization header field, the REGISTER should be resubmitted to the registrar.
